html:
Carcross/Tagish First Nation is the community of the Tagish and Inland Tlingit people around the lakes at the head of the Yukon River, in southern Yukon and northern British Columbia. Carcross is short for Caribou Crossing, where the herds once crossed between two lakes.

The Tagish spoke an Athabaskan language but traded and married with the coastal Tlingit, and many came to speak Tlingit. In 1896 a Tagish man, Keish, known as Skookum Jim, found gold on Bonanza Creek with his relatives Dawson Charlie, Kate Carmack and George Carmack. This set off the Klondike Gold Rush, which brought tens of thousands of miners through their land on the way to Dawson. See also the British Columbia part of the nation.
